hints: Look at where each pair of elements sits in Period 3, since most of these properties follow clear trends from left to right.
Recall that atomic radius decreases across the period, silicon is giant covalent with a very high boiling point, and phosphorus has extra stability from its half-filled 3p subshell.
Think about metallic bonding and how the number of delocalised electrons per atom affects how well a metal conducts electricity.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 context**

All four elements mentioned are in Period 3, from sodium on the left to chlorine on the right. This means we can use the standard trends in radius, structure, ionisation energy and metallic bonding.

Trend across Period 3 (Na to Cl): nuclear charge increases, shielding stays similar

**Check atomic radius: Al vs Si**

Across a period, greater proton number pulls the same shell in more strongly, so radius decreases. That means aluminium is larger than silicon, not the other way round.

$$\text{atomic radius: Na > Mg > Al > Si > P > S > Cl}$$

**Check boiling point: Cl vs Si**

Silicon has a giant covalent lattice with strong $\text{Si-Si}$ covalent bonds in all directions, needing huge energy to break. Chlorine is $\text{Cl}_2$ simple molecules with only weak van der Waals forces between them, so it is a gas.

$$\text{boiling point of Si (giant) >> boiling point of Cl}_2 \text{ (simple molecular)}$$

**Check first ionisation energy: P vs S**

General trend is increase across the period, but there is a famous dip at sulfur. Phosphorus has configuration $\text{[Ne] 3s}^2\text{3p}^3$ with a stable half-filled p subshell, while sulfur has $\text{[Ne] 3s}^2\text{3p}^4$ with paired electrons that repel.

$$\text{P: 3p}^3 \text{ (half-filled, more stable) > S: 3p}^4 \text{ (spin-pair repulsion)}$$

**Check conductivity: Mg vs Na**

Both are metals with delocalised electrons, but magnesium contributes two electrons per atom ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$) while sodium contributes only one ($\text{Na}^+$). More charge carriers with higher charge density gives stronger metallic bonding and better conductivity, so magnesium conducts better.

options.A: Incorrect. Atomic radius decreases across Period 3 due to increasing nuclear charge with similar shielding. Aluminium comes before silicon, so aluminium is larger than silicon.
options.B: Incorrect. Silicon has a giant covalent structure with a very high boiling point (around 3265 C), while chlorine exists as Cl2 molecules with weak intermolecular forces and boils at about -34 C. The trap is comparing non-metal to non-metal without checking structure type.
options.C: Incorrect. First ionisation energy of phosphorus is greater than that of sulfur. The 3p3 half-filled subshell in phosphorus is extra stable, and the paired electrons in sulfur's 3p4 cause repulsion that makes removal easier.
options.D: Correct. Both sodium and magnesium are metallic conductors, but magnesium releases 2 delocalised electrons per atom compared to 1 for sodium, and forms Mg2+ ions. This gives a higher concentration of mobile electrons and stronger metallic bonding, so magnesium has greater electrical conductivity.
